claim: Malaria caused an estimated 409,000 deaths in 2019.
source: Malaria is a major public health concern, with an estimated 409,000 deaths in 2019 (World Health Organization, 2020).
evidence: Cited from World Health Organization, 2020 report

claim: Human malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, with the majority of cases attributed to Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) and Plasmodium vivax (Pv).
source: Human malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, with the majority of cases attributed to Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) and Plasmodium vivax (Pv) (Lover et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Lover et al., 2018

claim: Pv is the predominant Plasmodium spp. in circulation for a majority of countries outside of Africa, accounting for ~75% of cases in South and North America, ~50% of cases in the Southeast Asia region, and ~30% in the Eastern Mediterranean region.
source: Pv is the predominant Plasmodium spp. in circulation for a majority of countries outside of Africa (~75% of cases in South and North America, ~50% of cases in the Southeast Asia region, and ~30% in the Eastern Mediterranean region; World Health Organization, 2020).
evidence: Cited from World Health Organization, 2020 report

claim: Pv infection can cause debilitating disease, including fever, myalgia, chronic anemia, reduced birthweight, and increased risk of neonatal death.
source: Despite overall lower mortality compared to Pf malaria, Pv infection can cause debilitating disease, including fever, myalgia, chronic anemia, reduced birthweight, and increased risk of neonatal death (Alexandre et al., 2010; Bardají et al., 2017; Genton et al., 2008).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Alexandre et al., 2010; Bardají et al., 2017; Genton et al., 2008)

claim: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of all Plasmodium sporozoites.
source: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of all Plasmodium sporozoites and is necessary for parasite development and infection (Cerami et al., 1992; Ménard et al., 1997; Nguitragool et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Cerami et al., 1992; Ménard et al., 1997; Nguitragool et al., 2017)

claim: CSP is necessary for parasite development and infection.
source: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of all Plasmodium sporozoites and is necessary for parasite development and infection (Cerami et al., 1992; Ménard et al., 1997; Nguitragool et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Cerami et al., 1992; Ménard et al., 1997; Nguitragool et al., 2017)

claim: CSP contains an unusual central region consisting of multiple, short amino acid repeats whose sequence depends on the Plasmodium species.
source: CSP contains an unusual central region consisting of multiple, short amino acid repeats whose sequence depends on the Plasmodium species (Chenet et al., 2012; Rich et al., 2000; Tahar et al., 1998).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Chenet et al., 2012; Rich et al., 2000; Tahar et al., 1998)

claim: The PvCSP central region is composed of nonapeptides GDRA(A/D)GQPA and ANGAGNQPG characteristic of strains VK210 and VK247, respectively.
source: The PvCSP central region is composed of nonapeptides GDRA(A/D)GQPA and ANGAGNQPG characteristic of strains VK210 and VK247, respectively (Arnot et al., 1985; Rosenberg et al., 1989; Figure 1A).
evidence: Cited from Arnot et al., 1985 and Rosenberg et al., 1989, and shown in Figure 1A

claim: PvCSP repeats are longer than Pf and Pb CSP repeats and consist primarily of glycine and alanine residues (~50% of all residues).
source: Unlike the 4-amino acid (aa)-long motifs of Pf and Plasmodium berghei (Pb) CSP, which are rich in asparagine and proline residues, PvCSP repeats are longer and consist primarily of glycine and alanine residues (~50% of all residues).
evidence: Direct comparison of sequence composition stated in the manuscript

claim: ~26% of the PvCSPvk210 central repeat region consists of charged residues, including arginine and aspartic acid residues.
source: Moreover, ~26% of the PvCSPvk210 central repeat region consists of charged residues, including arginine and aspartic acid residues.
evidence: Direct statement of sequence composition in the manuscript

claim: Both VK210 and VK247 strains have worldwide distribution.
source: Both VK210 and VK247 strains have worldwide distribution (Cheng et al., 2013; Kain et al., 1992; Soares et al., 2020), and VK210 appears to be a major target of the humoral immune response in studied populations (González et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2010; Soares et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Cheng et al., 2013; Kain et al., 1992; Soares et al., 2020)

claim: VK210 appears to be a major target of the humoral immune response in studied populations.
source: Both VK210 and VK247 strains have worldwide distribution (Cheng et al., 2013; Kain et al., 1992; Soares et al., 2020), and VK210 appears to be a major target of the humoral immune response in studied populations (González et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2010; Soares et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (González et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2010; Soares et al., 2020)

claim: The central region of CSP is immunodominant.
source: The central region of CSP is immunodominant, and antibodies targeting the repeats can inhibit sporozoite infection (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Mishra et al., 2012; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2017; Oyen et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2021; Potocnjak et al., 1980; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies

claim: Antibodies targeting the CSP repeats can inhibit sporozoite infection.
source: The central region of CSP is immunodominant, and antibodies targeting the repeats can inhibit sporozoite infection (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Mishra et al., 2012; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2017; Oyen et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2021; Potocnjak et al., 1980; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies

claim: The PfCSP central repeat is a major component of the most advanced malaria vaccine to date, RTS,S/AS01.
source: The PfCSP central repeat is a major component of the most advanced malaria vaccine to date, RTS,S/AS01 (Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018), and PvCSP or PvCSP-derived peptides are present in various clinical vaccine candidates against Pv (Mueller et al., 2009; Mueller et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from Adepoju, 2019 and Draper et al., 2018

claim: PvCSP or PvCSP-derived peptides are present in various clinical vaccine candidates against Pv.
source: The PfCSP central repeat is a major component of the most advanced malaria vaccine to date, RTS,S/AS01 (Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018), and PvCSP or PvCSP-derived peptides are present in various clinical vaccine candidates against Pv (Mueller et al., 2009; Mueller et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from Mueller et al., 2009 and Mueller et al., 2015

claim: Effective pre-erythrocytic stage vaccines are highly desirable to reduce the number of primary infections and prevent the establishment of hypnozoites that can lead to multiple relapses in Pv.
source: Effective pre-erythrocytic stage vaccines are highly desirable to reduce the number of primary infections, and in the case of Pv, to consequently prevent the establishment of hypnozoites that can lead to multiple relapses (Krotoski et al., 1982).
evidence: Cited from Krotoski et al., 1982

claim: A positive statistical association between the level of antibodies against the repeat region of PvCSP and protection has previously been established.
source: Although not much is known about the molecular basis of PvCSP recognition by inhibitory antibodies, a positive statistical association between the level of antibodies against the repeat region of PvCSP and protection has previously been established (Yadava et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from Yadava et al., 2014

claim: Anti-PvCSP species-specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) 2F2 and 2E10.E9 were generated in mice after immunization with radiation-attenuated Pv sporozoites of strains VK210 and VK247, respectively.
source: Anti-PvCSP species-specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) 2F2 and 2E10.E9 were generated in mice after immunization with radiation-attenuated Pv sporozoites of strains VK210 and VK247, respectively (Nardin et al., 1982).
evidence: Cited from Nardin et al., 1982

claim: Incubation of Pv sporozoites with mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 results in significantly reduced sporozoite infectivity.
source: Incubation of Pv sporozoites with mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 results in significantly reduced sporozoite infectivity, and thus despite a limited molecular understanding of their recognition, both antibodies have been valuable research tools in studies of Pv sporozoites (Cabrera-Mora et al., 2015; Gimenez et al., 2017; Miyazaki et al., 2020; Roth et al., 2018; Teixeira et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Cabrera-Mora et al., 2015; Gimenez et al., 2017; Miyazaki et al., 2020; Roth et al., 2018; Teixeira et al., 2014)

claim: Sporozoites attenuated with low concentrations of mAb 2F2 were significantly reduced in size and had lower DNA content, indicating post-hepatocyte-invasion antibody inhibition of liver stage development.
source: Interestingly, a recent study reported that sporozoites attenuated with low concentrations of mAb 2F2 were significantly reduced in size and had lower DNA content, indicating post-hepatocyte-invasion antibody inhibition of liver stage development (Roth et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Roth et al., 2018

claim: CD spectra of all analyzed PvCSP repeat peptides were indicative of a lack of secondary structure, with minima at ~200 nm.
source: CD spectra of all analyzed peptides were indicative of a lack of secondary structure, with minima at ~200 nm (Figure 1B).
evidence: CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 1B

claim: All analyzed PvCSP repeat peptides were highly disordered in solution and adopted a large ensemble of conformations.
source: All analyzed peptides were highly disordered in solution and adopted a large ensemble of conformations (Figure 2A), similar to peptides derived from PfCSP and PbCSP (Kucharska et al., 2020).
evidence: MD simulation data shown in Figure 2A and comparison to previous work

claim: Secondary structure in PvCSP repeat peptides was present mainly in the form of transient hydrogen-bonded β-turns.
source: Secondary structure was present mainly in the form of transient hydrogen-bonded β-turns (Figure 2B).
evidence: MD simulation data shown in Figure 2B

claim: PvCSPvk210 peptides displayed slightly lower averaged turn propensity (~15–20%) than PvCSPvk247 peptides (~23–26%).
source: The propensity of individual residues to form turns varied from 0 to ~60%, with PvCSPvk210 peptides displaying slightly lower averaged turn propensity (~15–20%) than PvCSPvk247 peptides (~23–26%) (Figure 2C).
evidence: MD simulation data shown in Figure 2C

claim: PvCSPvk210 peptides containing (GDRAAGQPA)2 motifs (210-7 and -9), as well as the last repeat of the 247-3 peptide (GNGAGGQAA), were the only motifs with a significant propensity to form helices (>20%).
source: PvCSPvk210 peptides containing (GDRAAGQPA)2 motifs (210-7 and -9), as well as the last repeat of the 247-3 peptide (GNGAGGQAA), were the only motifs with a significant propensity to form helices (>20%).
evidence: MD simulation analysis of secondary structure propensities

claim: PvCSP peptides behave like harmonic springs.
source: Calculations of elastic modulus demonstrated that PvCSP peptides behave like harmonic springs, meaning that the stretching or compressing of the peptides is proportional to the force applied to them.
evidence: Elastic modulus calculations from MD simulations

claim: The elastic modulus of PvCSP peptides was ~3–5 cal/(mol Å2).
source: On average, the elastic modulus was ~3–5 cal/(mol Å2), with the highest values (stiffest peptide) observed for peptide 247-2 (4.9 ± 0.2 cal/(mol Å2)) and lowest (most flexible peptide) observed for peptide 247-1 (3.2 ± 0.2 cal/(mol Å2)).
evidence: Elastic modulus calculations from MD simulations shown in Figure 2D

claim: Peptides 210-3 and 210-2 differ in the fifth residue of the first repeat, which is an aspartic acid for peptide 210-3 and an alanine for peptide 210-2 (GDRA(D/A)GQPA).
source: Peptides 210-3 and 210-2 differ in the fifth residue of the first repeat, which is an aspartic acid for peptide 210-3 and an alanine for peptide 210-2 (GDRA(D/A)GQPA).
evidence: Direct comparison of peptide sequences

claim: 2F2 recognizes the core epitope (2DRA(D/A)GQPAGD11) of all PvCSPvk210 peptides in an almost identical coil conformation with peptide backbone RMSD 0.10–0.28 Å.
source: 2F2 recognizes the core epitope (2DRA(D/A)GQPAGD11) of all PvCSPvk210 peptides in an almost identical coil conformation peptide backbone root-mean-square deviation (RMSD 0.10–0.28 Å) with two consecutive β-turns observed for residues 7QPAGD11 (Supplementary file 2) forming one turn of a 310-helix, thus consistent with the moderate secondary structure propensities observed for the unliganded PvCSPvk210 repeats (Figure 3B).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 3B

claim: Two consecutive β-turns observed for residues 7QPAGD11 form one turn of a 310-helix in 2F2-bound PvCSPvk210 peptides.
source: 2F2 recognizes the core epitope (2DRA(D/A)GQPAGD11) of all PvCSPvk210 peptides in an almost identical coil conformation peptide backbone root-mean-square deviation (RMSD 0.10–0.28 Å) with two consecutive β-turns observed for residues 7QPAGD11 (Supplementary file 2) forming one turn of a 310-helix, thus consistent with the moderate secondary structure propensities observed for the unliganded PvCSPvk210 repeats (Figure 3B).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The sidechains of D/A5 point up and away from the 2F2 paratope and do not significantly contribute to the 2F2 Fab-peptide interaction.
source: The sidechains of D/A5 point up and away from the 2F2 paratope and do not significantly contribute to the 2F2 Fab-peptide interaction, helping to explain the similar binding affinities to the different peptides containing this variation (Figure 3E).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 3E

claim: 2F2 binds the 210-5 peptide containing a unique repeat C-terminal of the central region (1GDRAAGQPAGNGAGGQAA18), but the electron density of residues 12–18 C-terminal of the bound core peptide motif is weak.
source: 2F2 also binds the 210-5 peptide containing a unique repeat C-terminal of the central region (1GDRAAGQPAGNGAGGQAA18); however, the electron density of residues 12–18 C-terminal of the bound core peptide motif is weak in the co-crystal structure, thus providing limited structural insight into this peptide region and suggesting it does not make strong interactions with 2F2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: Nine germline-encoded aromatic residues in 2F2 form significant van der Waals interactions with the peptides, contributing a total of ~385 Å2 of buried surface area.
source: 2F2 binds to PvCSPvk210 peptides using both germline and somatically hypermutated residues. Nine germline-encoded aromatic residues form significant van der Waals interactions with the peptides, contributing a total of ~385 Å2 of buried surface area (BSA; Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C, E, and G).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: The 2F2 paratope has an overall electronegative potential to accommodate arginine residues present in the sequence of the PvCSPvk210 peptides.
source: To accommodate arginine residues present in the sequence of the PvCSPvk210 peptides, the 2F2 paratope has an overall electronegative potential (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: Electrostatic potential analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A

claim: R3 and Q7 play a central role in mediating the 2F2 Fab-peptide interactions, forming six H-bonds with both heavy and light chain residues of the antibody.
source: R3 and Q7 play a central role in mediating the Fab-peptide interactions, forming six H-bonds with both heavy and light chain residues of the antibody (Figure 3E), and contributing ~107 Å2 and ~ 156 Å2 of BSA, respectively.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 3E

claim: 2E10.E9 Fab binds peptides derived from PvCSPvk247 with affinity ranging from 0.507 µM (peptide 247-4) to 1.67 µM (peptide 247-1).
source: 2E10.E9 Fab binds peptides derived from PvCSPvk247 with affinity ranging from 0.507 µM (peptide 247-4) to 1.67 µM (peptide 247-1), as measured by ITC.
evidence: ITC measurements shown in Figure 4A

claim: The 18-aa peptide 247-4 accommodates binding of one 2E10.E9 Fab, while 27-aa peptides 247-1, 247-2, and 247-3 are long enough to allow two Fabs to bind simultaneously.
source: Based on the binding stoichiometry derived from ITC, the 18-aa peptide 247-4 accommodates binding of one Fab, while 27-aa peptides 247-1, 247-2, and 247-3 are long enough to allow two Fabs to bind simultaneously (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: ITC stoichiometry data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: The core epitope of PvCSPvk247 peptides contains eight residues (3GAGNQPGA10) and adopts a similar coil conformation in all analyzed peptides when bound to 2E10.E9 (peptide backbone RMSD 0.48–1.0 Å).
source: The core epitope of PvCSPvk247 peptides contains eight residues (3GAGNQPGA10) and adopts a similar coil conformation in all analyzed peptides when bound to 2E10.E9 (peptide backbone RMSD 0.48–1.0 Å), with only isolated turns (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Six germline-encoded aromatic residues in 2E10.E9, including K.Tyr32, K.Tyr92, K.Tyr94, K.Phe96, H.Tyr32, and H.Trp50, play a central role in peptide recognition.
source: 2E10.E9 interacts with the PvCSPvk247 peptides using HCDRs 1, 2, and 3, and KCDR1 and 3, with the N-terminal part of the peptide positioned between HCDR1 and 3. Six germline-encoded aromatic residues, including K.Tyr32, K.Tyr92, K.Tyr94, K.Phe96, H.Tyr32, and H.Trp50, play a central role in peptide recognition, forming three H-bonds with G9, Ala10, and A13, and contributing 176 Å2 BSA to the relatively small paratope of this Fab (444 Å2 total BSA on the 2E10.E9 paratope; 588 Å2 total BSA on peptide 247-3) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, D, and F).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: HCDR3 H.Cys98 and H.Cys100 make a disulfide bond that positions H.Gly99 in an ideal position to form an H-bond with residue G9 of the peptide.
source: Interestingly, HCDR3 H.Cys98 and H.Cys100 make a disulfide bond that positions H.Gly99 in an ideal position to form an H-bond with residue G9 of the peptide and mimic the stacking effect provided by aromatic sidechains (Figure 4E).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: Residue N6 of the PvCSPvk247 peptides is central to the interaction with 2E10.E9, forming four H-bonds with HCDR2 residues H.Thr30, H.Asn52, and H.Ser52A.
source: Residue N6 of the PvCSPvk247 peptides is central to the interaction, forming four H-bonds with HCDR2 residues H.Thr30, H.Asn52, and H.Ser52A (Figure 4E).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: In the 2E10.E9 Fab-247-2 peptide co-crystal structure where two Fabs bind to one peptide, the two 2E10.E9 Fabs interact in a head-to-head binding mode at an ~146° angle.
source: In the 2E10.E9 Fab-247-2 peptide co-crystal structure where two Fabs bind to one peptide, we observed multiple contacts between the two 2E10.E9 Fabs (Figure 5). Indeed, the two 2E10.E9 Fabs interact in a head-to-head binding mode at an ~146o angle (Figure 5A).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 5A

claim: Contacts between the two 2E10.E9 Fabs are mostly symmetric and involve mainly HCDR2 of both Fab A and B, as well as the KCDR3 of Fab A.
source: Contacts between the two Fabs are mostly symmetric and involve mainly HCDR2 of both Fab A and B, as well as the KCDR3 of Fab A (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 5A and B

claim: Fab-Fab interactions in 2E10.E9 contribute 949 Å2 of BSA (482 Å2 on Fab A, 477 Å2 on Fab B).
source: Fab-Fab interactions contribute 949 Å2 of BSA (482 Å2 on Fab A, 477 Å2 on Fab B).
evidence: BSA calculation from X-ray crystal structure

claim: The interaction between neighboring 2E10.E9 Fabs is stabilized by five H-bonds; three between HCDR2 residues of both Fab A and B and two additional H-bonds between K.Tyr94 of Fab A, and H.Asn53 and H.Thr73 of Fab B.
source: The interaction between neighboring 2E10.E9 Fabs is stabilized by five H-bonds; three between HCDR2 residues of both Fab A and B and two additional H-bonds between K.Tyr94 of Fab A, and H.Asn53 and H.Thr73 of Fab B (Figure 5B).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 5B

claim: Only one of the residues involved in 2E10.E9 Fab-Fab contacts has been somatically hypermutated (H.Ser52A), making this homotypic Fab-Fab interaction primarily germline-encoded.
source: Comparison of the 2E10.E9 variable gene sequences to the inferred germline precursor (IGHV9-3 and IGKV8-19) reveals that only one of the residues involved in Fab-Fab contacts has been somatically hypermutated (H.Ser52A), making this homotypic Fab-Fab interaction primarily germline-encoded in the context of binding its repeating epitope (Figure 5C).
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 5C

claim: Both mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 exhibit fast associations to their respective PvCSP sequences.
source: Both mAbs exhibit fast associations to their respective PvCSP sequences, as revealed in biolayer interferometry (BLI) experiments (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: BLI data shown in Figure 6A and C

claim: mAb 2E10.E9 displays a relatively fast dissociation compared to mAb 2F2, which contributes to the lower overall binding affinity of this mAb to PvCSPvk247 compared to a higher binding affinity for the mAb 2F2-PvCSPvk210 interaction.
source: However, mAb 2E10.E9 displays a relatively fast dissociation compared to mAb 2F2, which contributes to the lower overall binding affinity of this mAb to PvCSPvk247 compared to a higher binding affinity for the mAb 2F2-PvCSPvk210 interaction.
evidence: BLI kinetics analysis

claim: 2F2 Fab recognizes PvCSPvk210 with ~10 times higher affinity (0.242 µM) compared to the 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 interaction (2.21 µM).
source: 2F2 Fab recognizes PvCSPvk210 with ~10 times higher affinity (0.242 µM) compared to the 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 interaction (2.21 µM), corroborating the binding kinetics data (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: ITC measurements shown in Figure 6B and D

claim: SEC-MALS characterization of the Fab-PvCSP complexes revealed high binding stoichiometry with a molecular weight of ~522 kDa and ~463 kDa for the 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk210 and 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complexes, respectively.
source: Size-exclusion chromatography coupled with multiangle light scattering (SEC-MALS) characterization of the Fab-PvCSP complexes revealed high binding stoichiometry with a molecular weight of ~522 kDa and ~463 kDa for the 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk210 and 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complexes, respectively (Figure 6E).
evidence: SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 6E

claim: The SEC-MALS molecular weights correspond to approximately 10 2F2 Fab's bound to one molecule of PvCSPvk210 and to approximately 9 2E10.E9 Fab's bound to one molecule of PvCSPvk247.
source: These sizes correspond to approximately 10 2F2 Fab's bound to one molecule of PvCSPvk210 and to approximately 9 2E10.E9 Fab's bound to one molecule of PvCSPvk247.
evidence: Calculation based on SEC-MALS molecular weight measurements

claim: 2D class average images from the negative stain micrographs of the 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex revealed multiple 2E10.E9 Fabs spaced tightly against each other.
source: 2D class average images from the negative stain micrographs of the 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex revealed multiple 2E10.E9 Fabs spaced tightly against each other (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, left panels).
evidence: NS EM data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A

claim: Cryo-EM analysis of the 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex indicated that Fab 2E10.E9 does not form regular, spiral assemblies with CSP.
source: However, cryo-EM analysis of the same 2E10.E9 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex indicated that Fab 2E10.E9 does not form regular, spiral assemblies with CSP, presumably because this type of complex would not accommodate the symmetric, head-to-head interactions between 2E10.E9 Fabs that were observed in the 2E10.E9 Fab-247-2 peptide crystal structure (Figure 5, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, right panels).
evidence: Cryo-EM data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and inference from crystal structure

claim: 2D classes from the negative stain micrographs of the 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk210 complex indicated multiple conformational states, suggesting that the PvCSPvk210 central repeat region remains largely flexible upon binding by 2F2 Fabs.
source: Interestingly, 2D classes from the negative stain micrographs of the 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk210 complex indicated multiple conformational states, and thereby suggest that the PvCSPvk210 central repeat region remains largely flexible upon binding by 2F2 Fabs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, left panels).
evidence: NS EM data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and inference from conformational heterogeneity

claim: Cryo-EM analysis of the 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex showed similar conformational heterogeneity.
source: Cryo-EM analysis of the same 2F2 Fab-PvCSPvk247 complex showed similar conformational heterogeneity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, right panels).
evidence: Cryo-EM data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B

claim: EM class averages from the micrographs of the 2F2 Fab-210-10 peptide complex displayed high variability in the angles between the two Fabs, ranging from ~30° to ~170°.
source: EM class averages from the micrographs of the 2F2 Fab-210-10 peptide complex displayed high variability in the angles between the two Fabs, ranging from ~30° to ~170° (Figure 7A).
evidence: EM data shown in Figure 7A

claim: The 2F2 Fab-210-10 peptide complex is highly flexible, and the two Fabs are likely not forming extensive stabilizing inter-Fab homotypic contacts upon binding the repeat peptide.
source: These data indicate that the complex is highly flexible, and that the two Fabs are likely not forming extensive stabilizing inter-Fab homotypic contacts upon binding the repeat peptide.
evidence: Inference from EM data showing high angular variability

claim: Complexes that form homotypic contacts (2E10.E9 Fab-247-2, 3D11 Fab-NPNDx2, and 1210 Fab-NANP5) showed lower flexibility than the 2F2 Fab-210-10 peptide complex, with either one or two distinct 3D classes present.
source: This mode of binding is in contrast to other Fab-peptide complexes known to form extensive homotypic interactions (2E10.E9 Fab-247-2 [Figure 7B], 3D11 Fab-NPNDx2 [Kucharska et al., 2020; Figure 7C], and 1210 Fab-NANP5 [Imkeller et al., 2018; Figure 7D, Supplementary file 1]). Complexes that form homotypic contacts showed lower flexibility than the 2F2 Fab-210-10 peptide complex, with either one or two distinct 3D classes present.
evidence: EM data shown in Figure 7B-D and comparison to 2F2 complex

claim: MD simulations on PvCSP-derived repeat peptides indicate that in the absence of interacting mAbs, the PvCSP repeat is largely disordered.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on PvCSP-derived repeat peptides indicate that in the absence of interacting mAbs, the PvCSP repeat is largely disordered.
evidence: MD simulation results presented in the manuscript

claim: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 lock PvCSP repeat peptides in a predominant coiled conformation, with antibody germline-encoded aromatic residues contributing significantly to the antigen contacts.
source: Our structural studies reveal how mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 lock PvCSP repeat peptides in a predominant coiled conformation, with antibody germline-encoded aromatic residues contributing significantly to the antigen contacts.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis presented in the manuscript

claim: mAb 2E10.E9 engages in head-to-head homotypic interactions when targeting PvCSP in a similar manner as previously described human mAbs against PfCSP and a murine mAb against PbCSP.
source: Moreover, we describe how mAb 2E10.E9 engages in head-to-head homotypic interactions when targeting PvCSP in a similar manner as previously described human mAbs against PfCSP (Imkeller et al., 2018; Oyen et al., 2018; Pholcharee et al., 2021) and a murine mAb against PbCSP (Kucharska et al., 2020).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis and comparison to previously published structures

claim: All analyzed PvCSP repeat peptides are disordered in solution and adopt a large ensemble of conformations, similar to peptides derived from PfCSP and PbCSP.
source: All analyzed peptides were highly disordered in solution and adopted a large ensemble of conformations (Figure 2A), similar to peptides derived from PfCSP and PbCSP (Kucharska et al., 2020).
evidence: MD simulation data and comparison to previous work

claim: The sequence composition of the CSP repeats from Pv, Pf, and Pb is substantially different; whereas PfCSP and PbCSP are asparagine and proline-rich, PvCSP is predominantly alanine and glycine-rich.
source: Interestingly, the sequence composition of the CSP repeats from these three Plasmodium species is substantially different; whereas PfCSP and PbCSP are asparagine and proline-rich, PvCSP is predominantly alanine and glycine-rich.
evidence: Sequence comparison stated in the manuscript

claim: The repeating modulus for PfCSP and PbCSP contains four amino acids, whereas the repeating modulus of PvCSP contains nine amino acids.
source: In addition, the repeating modulus for PfCSP and PbCSP contains four amino acids, whereas the repeating modulus of PvCSP contains nine amino acids.
evidence: Sequence comparison stated in the manuscript

claim: The elastic properties of PvCSP peptides likely stem from the combination of the low complexity periodic nature of the sequence as well as the particular amino acid composition of this region.
source: The high degree of conformational disorder and the resulting elastic properties of PvCSP peptides likely stem from the combination of the low complexity periodic nature of the sequence as well as the particular amino acid composition of this region.
evidence: Inference from MD simulation results and sequence analysis

claim: A high combined proline and glycine content distinguishes the sequence of self-assembled elastomeric proteins such as elastin, resilin, and elastic spider silks from that of proteins prone to amyloid formation.
source: A high combined proline and glycine content was shown to distinguish the sequence of self-assembled elastomeric proteins such as elastin, resilin, and elastic spider silks, amongst many others, from that of proteins prone to amyloid formation (Rauscher et al., 2006).
evidence: Cited from Rauscher et al., 2006

claim: Both proline and glycine are 'amyloid breakers' because of their low propensity to form regular secondary structure such as the extended β-sheets found at the core of amyloid fibrils.
source: Both proline and glycine are 'amyloid breakers' because of their low propensity to form regular secondary structure such as the extended β-sheets found at the core of amyloid fibrils (Parrini et al., 2005; Williams et al., 2004).
evidence: Cited from Parrini et al., 2005 and Williams et al., 2004

claim: PvCSP peptides have glycine and proline contents of ~22–33% and ~7–11%, respectively, and are predicted to fall within the transition region separating amyloidogenic from elastomeric proteins.
source: PvCSP peptides have glycine and proline contents of ~22–33% and ~7–11%, respectively, and thus are predicted to fall within the transition region separating amyloidogenic from elastomeric proteins, the latter of which include elastin domains and insect resilin (Rauscher et al., 2006).
evidence: Sequence composition analysis and comparison to Rauscher et al., 2006

claim: The elastic modulus of PvCSP peptides (~3–5 cal/(mol Å2)) is commensurate with the elastic modulus of peptides modeled after human elastin (~9 cal/(mol Å2)).
source: Moreover, the elastic modulus of PvCSP peptides (~3–5 cal/(mol Å2)) is commensurate with the elastic modulus of peptides modeled after human elastin (~9 cal/(mol Å2)), which requires extensibility and elasticity for its physiological function (Reichheld et al., 2021).
evidence: Comparison of elastic modulus values to Reichheld et al., 2021

claim: Achieving a high degree of conformational disorder may be an essential aspect of CSP function on the surface of sporozoites.
source: This analogy supports the observation that CSP is inherently elastic and suggests that achieving a high degree of conformational disorder may be an essential aspect of CSP function on the surface of sporozoites.
evidence: Inference from elastic properties and comparison to elastomeric proteins

claim: Recent in vitro experiments demonstrated that PbCSP repeats have elastic properties, which are lost when the repeat sequence is scrambled.
source: Interestingly, recent in vitro experiments demonstrated that PbCSP repeats also have elastic properties, which are lost when the repeat sequence is scrambled (Balaban et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from Balaban et al., 2021

claim: Biophysical properties of the CSP repeats are necessary for maintaining sporozoite motility.
source: The link between the elasticity of CSP repeats and CSP function is still not completely understood; yet, it appears that biophysical properties of the CSP repeats are necessary for maintaining sporozoite motility (Balaban et al., 2021; Coppi et al., 2011), even though CSP itself is not a motor protein.
evidence: Cited from Balaban et al., 2021 and Coppi et al., 2011

claim: Inhibitory mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 recognize their epitopes in an induced coil conformation, with only one turn of a 310-helix and isolated turns as secondary structure motifs.
source: The presence of disorder in all analyzed PvCSP repeat peptide structures was also appreciated in our X-ray crystallography data, where inhibitory mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 were found to recognize their epitopes in an induced coil conformation, with only one turn of a 310-helix and isolated turns as secondary structure motifs observed in both instances.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis

claim: Binding of the CSP repeat by inhibitory antibodies has been shown to induce a range of conformations in this intrinsically disordered region for Pf and Pb.
source: Binding of the CSP repeat by inhibitory antibodies has been shown to induce a range of conformations in this intrinsically disordered region for Pf and Pb, with the occasional presence of type I β-turns and pseudo 310-turns often but not always linked with antibody-mediated protection (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Kucharska et al., 2020; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2017; Pholcharee et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2021; Scally and Julien, 2018; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies

claim: PfCSP- and PbCSP-reactive antibodies have been shown to cross-react to a varying extent with the predominant repeat motif and neighboring sequences of subtle variance within the repeat region.
source: PfCSP- and PbCSP-reactive antibodies have been shown to cross-react to a varying extent with the predominant repeat motif and neighboring sequences of subtle variance within the repeat region, for example, the PfCSP junction (Julien and Wardemann, 2019; Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Scally et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies

claim: Cross-reactivity is a feature of human antibodies encoded by various Ig-gene combinations and was also observed in murine antibodies against the PfCSP repeat (mAb 2A10) and against the PbCSP repeat (3D11).
source: Cross-reactivity is a feature of human antibodies encoded by various Ig-gene combinations and was also observed in murine antibodies against the PfCSP repeat (mAb 2A10; Zavala et al., 1983) and against the PbCSP repeat (3D11; Kucharska et al., 2020; Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies

claim: Both mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are cross-reactive as they bind to different repeat motifs of their respective PvCSP variants with similar affinity and in identical conformations.
source: Our data indicate that both mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are cross-reactive as they bind to different repeat motifs of their respective PvCSP variants with similar affinity and in identical conformations.
evidence: ITC and X-ray crystal structure data presented in the manuscript

claim: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are not cross-reactive to different strains of Pv due to the significantly different CSP sequences of strains PvCSPvk210 and PvCSPvk247.
source: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are, however, not cross-reactive to different strains of Pv (Nardin et al., 1982) due to the significantly different CSP sequences of strains PvCSPvk210 and PvCSPvk247.
evidence: Cited from Nardin et al., 1982 and sequence comparison

claim: Only mAb 2F2 was reported to induce aberrations in size and in DNA content of sporozoites, indicating a distinct mechanism of attenuation.
source: Although both mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are inhibitory, only mAb 2F2 was reported to induce aberrations in size and in DNA content of sporozoites, indicating a distinct mechanism of attenuation (Roth et al., 2018), possibly due to the higher affinity to PvCSP and slower dissociation rate of mAb 2F2 compared to mAb 2E10.E9.
evidence: Cited from Roth et al., 2018 and inference from binding kinetics data

claim: The difference in affinities between mAbs 2E10.E9 and 2F2 and their respective antigen might partially stem from the low number of somatic hypermutations of mAb 2E10.E9 (1 in HC, 6 in KC) compared to 2F2 (14 in HC, 4 in KC).
source: The difference in affinities between mAbs 2E10.E9 and 2F2 and their respective antigen might partially stem from the low lumber of somatic hypermutations of mAb 2E10.E9 (1 in HC, 6 in KC) compared to 2F2 (14 in HC, 4 in KC).
evidence: Sequence analysis and inference from affinity differences

claim: Germline-encoded mAb 2E10.E9 residue H.Trp50 forms extensive van der Waals interactions with N6 and P8 residues, analogous to IGHV3-33 germline-encoded H.Trp52 in several human mAbs.
source: Specifically, mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 use nine and six germline-encoded aromatic residues, respectively, to mediate contacts with their core epitopes. Germline-encoded mAb 2E10.E9 residue H.Trp50 forms extensive van der Waals interactions with N6 and P8 residues, analogous to IGHV3-33 germline-encoded H.Trp52 in several human mAbs, including mAbs MGG4 (Tan et al., 2018), 1210 (Imkeller et al., 2018), 311 (Oyen et al., 2017), and other antibodies induced by sporozoite immunization (Murugan et al., 2020) or RTS,S vaccination (Pholcharee et al., 2021; Figure 3—figure supplement 3D and F).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis and comparison to previously published structures

claim: It is likely that CSP repeats prime the mammalian immune system to select antibodies from germline genes with already optimally positioned aromatic residues.
source: As both human and murine mAbs appear to depend on germline-encoded aromatic residues for CSP recognition, it is likely that CSP repeats prime the mammalian immune system to select antibodies from germline genes with already optimally positioned aromatic residues.
evidence: Inference from structural analysis of multiple antibodies

claim: MAb 2E10.E9 displays homotypic Fab-Fab interactions, as was previously described for mAbs 1210, 311, 239, and 399 against PfCSP and murine mAb 3D11 against PbCSP.
source: MAb 2E10.E9 displays homotypic Fab-Fab interactions, as was previously described for mAbs 1210 (Imkeller et al., 2018), 311 (Oyen et al., 2018), and 239 and 399 (Pholcharee et al., 2021) against PfCSP and murine mAb 3D11 against PbCSP (Kucharska et al., 2020).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis and comparison to previously published structures

claim: 2E10.E9 Fabs interact in a head-to-head binding mode, forming symmetric interactions similar to those observed in the case of antibodies 1210 and 399.
source: 2E10.E9 Fabs interact in a head-to-head binding mode, forming symmetric interactions similar to those observed in the case of antibodies 1210 (Imkeller et al., 2018) and 399 (Pholcharee et al., 2021).
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis and comparison to previously published structures

claim: mAb 2E10.E9 does not appear to bind longer PvCSPvk247 peptides with higher affinity compared to shorter PvCSPvk247 peptides, in contrast to what has been described for other mAbs that recognize the PfCSP and PbCSP repeats and form homotypic interactions.
source: Interestingly, mAb 2E10.E9 does not appear to bind longer PvCSPvk247 peptides with higher affinity compared to shorter PvCSPvk247 peptides (Figure 3A), in contrast to what has been described for other mAbs that recognize the PfCSP and PbCSP repeats and form homotypic interactions (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kucharska et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2021).
evidence: ITC data and comparison to previously published studies

claim: The residues forming Fab-Fab contacts in mAb 2E10.E9 are almost exclusively germline-encoded, similar to mAb 399.
source: Unlike mAbs 1210 (Imkeller et al., 2018) and 3D11 (Kucharska et al., 2020), the residues forming Fab-Fab contacts in mAb 2E10.E9 are almost exclusively germline-encoded, similar to mAb 399 (Pholcharee et al., 2021).
evidence: Sequence analysis and comparison to previously published structures

claim: Forming Fab-Fab interactions is ubiquitous among anti-CSP mAbs targeting different Plasmodium species.
source: Combined, these results suggest that forming Fab-Fab interactions is ubiquitous among anti-CSP mAbs targeting different Plasmodium species.
evidence: Inference from structural analysis of multiple antibodies across species

claim: NANP homotypic antibody interactions promote activation and strong clonal expansion of PfCSP-reactive B-cells.
source: Analysis of human mAbs isolated after immunization with whole Pf sporozoites indicated that NANP homotypic antibody interactions promote activation and strong clonal expansion of PfCSP-reactive B-cells (Imkeller et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Imkeller et al., 2018

claim: Homotypic interactions may emerge from B-cell receptor clustering on the surface of B cells.
source: It appears that homotypic interactions may emerge from B-cell receptor clustering on the surface of B cells (Imkeller et al., 2018); however, a direct link between homotypic interactions in the context of soluble antibodies and sporozoite inhibition is still to be established.
evidence: Cited from Imkeller et al., 2018 with caveat about direct link

claim: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 recognize core PvCSP epitopes of 10 and 8 residues, respectively.
source: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 recognize core PvCSP epitopes of 10 and 8 residues, respectively.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis

claim: Potent inhibitory mAbs against PfCSP and PbCSP typically recognize epitopes of similar length (8–10 residues), despite shorter repeating motifs for PfCSP and PbCSP (4-aa) compared to PvCSP (9-aa).
source: Interestingly, potent inhibitory mAbs against PfCSP and PbCSP typically recognize epitopes of similar length (8–10 residues; Imkeller et al., 2018; Kucharska et al., 2020; Murugan et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2021), despite shorter repeating motifs for PfCSP and PbCSP (4-aa) compared to PvCSP (9-aa).
evidence: Comparison to previously published studies

claim: Similar CSP-based vaccine design approaches could be applied across different Plasmodium species.
source: Given the similar antibody epitope lengths, in addition to similar structural propensities for underlying antigenic motifs and induction of antibody homotypic interactions when recognizing closely spaced repeating epitopes, we suggest that similar CSP-based vaccine design approaches could be applied across different Plasmodium species.
evidence: Inference from structural similarities across species

claim: The lack of Plasmodium species cross-reactivity for the potent inhibitory mAbs described thus far suggests that different pre-erythrocytic vaccines or a multicomponent CSP-based vaccine will likely be required for broad coverage against the different Plasmodium species causative of human malaria morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Nevertheless, the lack of Plasmodium species cross-reactivity for the potent inhibitory mAbs described thus far suggests that different pre-erythrocytic vaccines or a multicomponent CSP-based vaccine will likely be required for broad coverage against the different Plasmodium species causative of human malaria morbidity and mortality worldwide.
evidence: Inference from lack of cross-species reactivity

claim: Eight crystal structures were solved to unveil the interactions of two inhibitory monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), 2F2 and 2E10.E9, with PvCSP repeats.
source: Next, we solved eight crystal structures to unveil the interactions of two inhibitory monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), 2F2 and 2E10.E9, with PvCSP repeats.
evidence: X-ray crystallography data presented in the manuscript

claim: Both antibodies 2F2 and 2E10.E9 can accommodate subtle sequence variances in the repeat motifs.
source: Both antibodies can accommodate subtle sequence variances in the repeat motifs and recognize largely coiled peptide conformations that also contain isolated turns.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis showing binding to different peptide variants

claim: Both antibodies 2F2 and 2E10.E9 recognize largely coiled peptide conformations that also contain isolated turns.
source: Both antibodies can accommodate subtle sequence variances in the repeat motifs and recognize largely coiled peptide conformations that also contain isolated turns.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis

claim: The structural studies uncover various degrees of Fab-Fab homotypic interactions upon recognition of the PvCSP central repeats by these two inhibitory mAbs, similar to potent mAbs against PfCSP.
source: Our structural studies uncover various degrees of Fab-Fab homotypic interactions upon recognition of the PvCSP central repeats by these two inhibitory mAbs, similar to potent mAbs against PfCSP.
evidence: X-ray crystal structure analysis and comparison to PfCSP mAbs
